exploit_name: BuilderWallet init() unprotected re-initialization allows admin takeover and fund theft
description: The init() function lacks access control and initialization guards, allowing repeated calls that overwrite the builderAdmin state variable. Attacker calls init(attacker_address) to seize admin, then sweep() to drain funds.
attack_scenario: 1) Builder wallet deployed and accumulates fees. 2) Attacker calls init(attacker) to become admin. 3) Attacker calls sweep(token, attacker) to extract all balances.
root_cause: The init() function lacks access control and initialization guards, allowing repeated calls that overwrite the builderAdmin state variable. Attacker calls init(attacker_address) to seize admin, then sweep() to drain funds.
fix_description: Implement access control on init() and add an initialization guard (require(!initialized)) to ensure single execution.
notes: Direct theft of all ERC20 balances held by any builder wallet including protocol-distributed fees/shares.
